rows.unsupported_part: The definition of "arm's length terms and conditions" is not stated in the passages; the only passage provided defines "tax".

Table I setting Class 3 at a rate of 25%, and listing Motor Vehicle Expenditure as qualifying capital expenditure in Class 3, are not stated in the passage. The only passage provided is paragraph 10 on the value of an asset at disposal, which does not mention Table I, capital allowance classes, rates, or motor vehicles.

The statement that a company must file a self-assessment return with the Service, in the prescribed form, at least once a year, whether or not it is liable to pay tax. The passage does not state this obligation. It refers to subsection (2), which is not included, and only sets filing deadlines in subsection (5) and an exclusion from subsection (2) for certain non-resident companies.
The relevant tax authority may make rules or regulations for the administration of this section. The passage contains no power for any tax authority to make rules or regulations.

The statement that the Service may, by notice, appoint any person, including a non-resident supplier, to collect VAT and remit it to the Service. The passage only covers fiscalisation of supplies (implementation of the fiscalisation system and its possible components) and says nothing about appointing collection agents, notices, or non-resident suppliers.

The statement says section 21 bars a deduction for any tax or penalty borne on behalf of another person. The passages cover only section 20(1)(i) to (m) and say nothing about section 21 or about tax or penalties borne for another person.

The statement that a small company's return may contain a statement of accounts attested to by the taxpayer in place of audited financial statements. The passages cover only filing times for companies and representatives (section 11(3) to (6)) and say nothing about small companies, the content of returns, or attested accounts in place of audited statements.

The statement says the rule does not apply to distributions by a real estate investment company from rental and dividend income received for shareholders, whether from current or previous periods' profits. The passage (section 7) defines Nigerian dividends and their timing but says nothing about real estate investment companies or any exclusion for them.
